outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no accepted or independently checked result settles the problem; the new material is an unvalidated 798-page single-author claim of a full proof for perfect base fields (Chenxiao Tian, arXiv 2608.20066, 20 August 2026), an author-led 2025–2026 series by Yi Hu re-presenting a 2022 claim of resolution in arbitrary characteristic (partly corrected by the author, with no independent check found), and an AI-assisted paper (Gergely Bérczi, arXiv 2602.06553, using AlphaEvolve and GPT 5.2 Pro) that gives conjectural ranking functions for dimension 4 in characteristic 3 without any resolution claim.
problem_asks: Whether every algebraic variety over a field of characteristic p (for each prime p) admits resolution of singularities, meaning a proper birational morphism from a regular (smooth) scheme that is an isomorphism over the regular locus. Unpacked: (1) the existence of resolution for varieties of every dimension, not only dimensions up to 3; (2) over every field of characteristic p, and the bullet does not say perfect; (3) for every prime p. The bullet asks for resolution (desingularisation) and does not in its own words ask for embedded resolution, principalisation or functoriality, although the usual formulations include them. The Wikipedia lead (fetched 2026) states the open case as varieties of dimension at least 4 over fields of characteristic p; the dimension 1 to 3 cases are recorded as known (see events). Nothing in the bullet narrows it to a particular dimension or field, so the open content is every dimension at least 4 over every field of characteristic p.

events.what_happened: Abhyankar's resolution of algebraic surfaces over fields of any nonzero characteristic (title: 'Local uniformization on algebraic surfaces over ground fields of characteristic p ≠ 0'), as cited in the Wikipedia article and in the Proof Atlas reference list. Old classical result; not re-read from the original.
events.delivers: Resolution for surfaces (dimension 2) over fields of any nonzero characteristic. Restricted to dimension 2.
events.remains: Every dimension 3 and up, which is the bullet's question.
events.direction: Confirms the problem in dimension 2; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Abhyankar's 1966 proof of resolution for 3-folds in positive characteristic. Wikipedia gives the characteristic bound as greater than 6; Cutkosky's 2006 abstract says Abhyankar's first proof was in 1966 for the theorem stated there in characteristic greater than 5. The two sources state the bound differently and I did not resolve which is right.
events.delivers: Resolution for 3-folds in positive characteristic greater than 6 (per Wikipedia). Restricted to dimension 3 and to large characteristic.
events.remains: 3-folds in characteristic 6 or less (taken up by the Cossart–Piltant results), and every dimension 4 and up.
events.doubts: The characteristic bound differs between sources (greater than 6 in Wikipedia; Cutkosky's abstract refers to greater than 5 in his own proof and attributes the first proof to Abhyankar in 1966).
events.direction: Confirms the problem for 3-folds in large positive characteristic; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Lipman's extension of the surface result to all excellent 2-dimensional schemes, as recorded in the Wikipedia article. Classical; not re-read from the original.
events.delivers: Resolution for all excellent 2-dimensional schemes. Restricted to dimension 2.
events.remains: Dimension 3 and up.
events.direction: Confirms the problem in dimension 2; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Marc Spivakovsky announced in May 1992 a proof of the general case of resolution in positive characteristic, according to T.T. Moh's undated page at Purdue. The same page says the manuscript was still being written (originally expected to be about 23 pages), that 'many people (mostly non-experts), who have access to some versions of his manuscript, judge unfavourably', and that 'It is anybody's guess if the proof is correct'. I found no manuscript or publication.
events.delivers: Claimed a proof of the general case (all dimensions, positive characteristic, as relayed on the Moh page). Nothing written that I could read.
events.remains: Everything, if the claim is not valid.
events.doubts: Moh's page reports that people who saw versions judged them unfavourably (described there as mostly non-experts), and the manuscript was still unfinished when the page was written. No published version or verification was found.
events.direction: Claimed proof of the general case, cutting in favour of resolution if correct.

events.what_happened: Tohsuke Urabe, 'New Ideas for Resolution of Singularities in Arbitrary Characteristics', arXiv math/0006071 (v1 9 June 2000). The abstract claims every two-dimensional hypersurface singularity in any characteristic can be resolved by iterated monoidal transformations with centres in smooth subvarieties, and that extension to higher dimensions 'seems to be possible' if several further ideas are added. The author withdrew it: v2 (18 June 2010) carries the notice 'This paper has been withdrawn by Tohsuke Urabe.'
events.delivers: Claimed resolution of two-dimensional hypersurface singularities in any characteristic (dimension 2 only). Withdrawn by the author; the claim is no longer offered as a result.
events.remains: Dimension 3 and up, and the general case.
events.doubts: Withdrawn by its author; no reason is given on the arXiv page.

withdrawn.what: The 2000 claim (arXiv math/0006071), withdrawn in its v2 with the notice 'This paper has been withdrawn by the author.' No reason stated.

events.direction: Claimed partial result (dimension 2), since withdrawn.

events.what_happened: Steven Dale Cutkosky, 'Resolution of Singularities for 3-folds in positive characteristic', arXiv math/0606530. Abstract: 'a concise, complete proof of resolution of singularities of 3-folds in positive characteristic (>5) is given. The first proof of this theorem was given by Abhyankar in 1966.' v1 21 June 2006; the comments say the final version (v4, 14 Nov 2007) is 'to appear in the American Journal of Mathematics' (acceptance not confirmed by me).
events.revisions: v2 11 Aug 2006; v3 9 Dec 2006; v4 14 Nov 2007 (current, 'to appear in the American Journal of Mathematics').
events.delivers: Resolution for 3-folds over positive characteristic greater than 5 (dimension 3 only, with the characteristic restriction stated in the title and abstract). The resolution morphism is an isomorphism over the nonsingular locus.
events.remains: 3-folds in characteristic 5 or less, which the Cossart–Piltant results cover (see those events), and every dimension 4 and up.
events.direction: Confirms the problem for 3-folds in characteristic greater than 5; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Vincent Cossart and Olivier Piltant, 'Resolution of singularities of threefolds in positive characteristic I' (J. Algebra 320 (2008) 1051–1082) and 'II' (J. Algebra 321 (2009) 1836–1976). The HAL abstract (search snippet, HAL page blocked) states the aim as resolution of 3-dimensional varieties over a field k of characteristic p>0 'whenever k is differentially finite over some perfect subfield k0'. Part I reduces the threefold problem to local uniformisation for Artin–Schreier and purely inseparable coverings. The HAL deposit date could not be retrieved, so the date given is the journal year, which may be later than the first public write-up.
events.delivers: Resolution for quasiprojective 3-dimensional schemes over positive characteristic fields that are differentially finite over a perfect subfield (per the HAL abstract). Restricted to dimension 3 and to that class of fields. The Wikipedia summary says 'in all characteristics'; the HAL abstract imposes the differential-finiteness condition. I read the HAL abstract only through a search snippet.
events.remains: Dimension 4 and up; 3-folds over fields that are not differentially finite over a perfect field (taken up by the 2014 arithmetical paper, see below). Embedded resolution of 3-folds is also reported open in the Matsuki 2019 Kyoto abstract, though the bullet does not ask for embedded resolution.

checked_by.who: Journal of Algebra (refereeing process; referees not named in what I could read)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published Part I (vol. 320, 2008) and Part II (vol. 321, 2009); volume details come from search snippets and the Wikipedia reference list

events.doubts: The scope is narrower than the Wikipedia summary, as noted under 'delivers'. I did not read the papers themselves.
events.direction: Proves resolution for threefolds in positive characteristic, under the differential-finiteness hypothesis; cuts in favour of resolution in dimension 3 only.

events.what_happened: Peter Woit's blog post 'Proof of Resolution of Singularities in Characteristic p?' (dated 23 Sept 2008) reported second-hand that Heisuke Hironaka had been giving talks at Harvard 'claiming to have a proof that singularities of algebraic varieties can be resolved for any dimension in characteristic p'. Woit did not know the details. Commenter Terry Hughes (23 Sept 2008) called it 'a vast overstatement', saying Hironaka 'outlined a new approach at Harvard, but made no claims that he solved the problem'. Woit's update says his source 'was most likely overly optimistic' and that 'several groups are working on this... with no definitive proof yet done'. The talks themselves are not dated in the sources; the date given is that of the blog report.
events.revisions: Woit's update, same post, states the claim was probably overstated.
events.delivers: A reported claim, relayed second-hand, of resolution in positive characteristic in all dimensions. No written argument from this announcement was found. The update and the commenters say the claim was overstated.
events.remains: Everything, if the talks made no claim of a solution.
events.doubts: Second-hand; no written version from the talks found; the blog's own update weakens the claim; the Matsuki 2019 Kyoto abstract says that nobody has been able to confirm the details of Hironaka's alleged proof.
events.direction: As relayed, a claim of the full problem; as corrected by the update and commenters, an outline of an approach with no claimed solution. This is a disputed reading of the same event.

events.what_happened: Vincent Cossart and Olivier Piltant, 'Resolution of Singularities of Arithmetical Threefolds', arXiv 1412.0868 (v1 2 Dec 2014; v2 8 Jan 2019, 'updates and extends' an earlier posting). The abstract: 'We prove Grothendieck's Conjecture on Resolution of Singularities for quasi-excellent schemes X of dimension three and of arbitrary characteristic.' It applies to 'algebraic or arithmetical varieties of dimension three'. No journal reference is listed on the arXiv page.
events.delivers: Resolution for all dimension-3 quasi-excellent schemes in arbitrary characteristic, which includes dimension-3 varieties over arbitrary fields of positive characteristic, with no differential-finiteness condition. Restricted to dimension 3.
events.remains: Every dimension 4 and up, for positive characteristic varieties.
events.time_since_posted: about 11 years 10 months (v1); about 7 years 9 months (v2)
events.direction: Cuts in favour of resolution, in dimension 3 and all characteristics.

events.what_happened: Hironaka posted to his personal webpage a manuscript 'Resolution of singularities in positive characteristics' (Harvard PDF; Wikipedia's reference was retrieved 17 May 2017). Wikipedia says it 'claims to prove the existence of a resolution of singularities in a positive characteristic'. The Proof Atlas reference list describes it as one of the 'all-dimensional results' that the page says 'have not been validated'. I could not read the PDF (the fetch returned compressed binary), so the scope and argument are not checked by me.
events.delivers: Claimed (per Wikipedia and the Proof Atlas reference list) resolution in positive characteristic, all dimensions per Proof Atlas. Not confirmed from the text.
events.remains: Unknown from my reading.
events.doubts: Wikipedia does not say whether the claim has been verified, accepted or refuted. The Proof Atlas page says the collection's all-dimensional claims are not validated. Matsuki's 2019 Kyoto abstract says nobody has confirmed the details of Hironaka's alleged positive-characteristic proof. I could not read the manuscript.
events.direction: Claims a proof of existence, cutting in favour of resolution if correct.

events.what_happened: Herwig Hauser and Stefan Perlega, 'Cycles of Singularities appearing in the Resolution Problem in positive Characteristic', arXiv 1802.05010 (14 Feb 2018), 'to appear in the Journal of Algebraic Geometry'. It exhibits a hypersurface singularity defined by a purely inseparable power series and a sequence of point blowups after which a similar singularity reappears with some exponents shifted upward, a cycle. It disproves a theorem claimed by Moh on the stability of the residual order under blowup sequences. The abstract says: 'It is not a counter-example to the resolution in positive characteristic since larger centers are also permissible.'
events.revisions: Journal of Algebraic Geometry (listed as 'to appear' in the arXiv comments).
events.delivers: A cycle of point-blowup sequences for the residual-order invariant in positive characteristic, which disproves a stated theorem of Moh about that invariant. By the authors' own statement it is not a counterexample to resolution, because larger centres remain permissible. It concerns one invariant and one choice of centres.
events.remains: The whole question; it neither settles nor counters existence of resolution.
events.direction: Neutral to the answer: shows that one candidate invariant can cycle under point blowups, and the authors say it does not counter resolution.
events.object: A hypersurface singularity in positive characteristic defined by a purely inseparable power series, with a finite sequence of point blowups after which the same type of singularity reappears with some exponents shifted up. Explicit (given in the paper, which I did not reproduce from the abstract page).

events.what_happened: Two versions of what appears to be one result on embedded resolution of surface singularities in arbitrary characteristic. (a) Stefan Perlega, 'A New Proof for the Embedded Resolution of Surface Singularities in Arbitrary Characteristic', arXiv 2011.14443 (29 Nov 2020), handed in as a doctoral thesis at the University of Vienna. Abstract: surfaces in a three-dimensional smooth ambient space over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic, using an upper semicontinuous resolution invariant. (b) Herwig Hauser and Stefan Perlega, 'Resolving Surface Singularities in Positive Characteristic', Publ. RIMS 60(4) (2024), 767–813 (DOI 10.4171/PRIMS/60-4-5), submitted 16 Feb 2022 and published 7 Nov 2024; abstract: 'a systematic proof for the embedded resolution of two-dimensional hypersurface singularities over a field of arbitrary characteristic'. I have not verified that (a) and (b) contain the same argument. The date given is for (a) as the earliest public written version of this subject; if they are different arguments, the date for (b) would be its publication date, 2024-11-07.
events.revisions: Published as Hauser–Perlega, Publ. RIMS 60(4) (2024), submitted 16 Feb 2022 and published 7 Nov 2024. Overlap with arXiv 2011.14443 not verified.
events.delivers: Embedded resolution of surface (dimension 2) singularities in arbitrary characteristic, per both versions. Surfaces were already known (Abhyankar 1956, Lipman 1978), so this is a new proof for a known case, not an extension in dimension.
events.remains: Dimension 3 and up.

checked_by.who: Publications of the Research Institute for Mathematical Sciences (Kyoto); referees not named on the page
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the Hauser–Perlega paper on 7 Nov 2024 after submission on 16 Feb 2022

events.direction: Cuts in favour of resolution for surfaces, a case already known; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Yi Hu, 'Grassmannians and Singularities', arXiv 2109.02968 (v1 7 Sep 2021; v4 8 Mar 2022; 148 pages). Abstract: 'Let X be an integral scheme of finite presentation over a perfect field. Let q be a singular closed point of X.' The claim is that some open V containing q admits a resolution. Hu gave a talk, 'Local Resolution of Singularities', on 5 Nov 2021 (seminar listing, University of California San Diego; speaker listed as University of Arizona).
events.revisions: v2 1 Oct 2021; v3 12 Oct 2021; v4 8 Mar 2022. Its comments say the 2022 paper supersedes it.
events.delivers: Local resolution only: for each singular closed point q of an integral finite-presentation scheme over a perfect field, some open neighbourhood V of q admits a resolution. Global resolution of X is not claimed.
events.remains: Global resolution of X, and every restriction the 2022 paper removes.
events.doubts: Superseded by the 2022 paper per its comments. No outside engagement found.
events.direction: Cuts in favour of local resolution, a restricted version of the question.

events.what_happened: Yi Hu, 'Resolution of Singularities in Arbitrary Characteristic', arXiv 2203.03842 (v1 8 Mar 2022; v2 30 Mar 2022; v3 24 Jun 2022; v4 1 Aug 2022; 141 pages). Abstract: 'Let X be an integral affine or projective scheme of finite presentation over a perfect field. We prove that X admits a resolution, that is, there exists a smooth scheme X̃ and a projective birational morphism from X̃ onto X.' Comments: 'Added ell blowups'; the method is restructured and the proofs simplified and shortened. No journal reference, no DOI beyond the arXiv one, and no withdrawal notice on the abstract page. A talk with the same title was listed for the Stanford algebraic geometry seminar on 25 Feb 2022 (listing seen in search, not opened).
events.revisions: v2 30 Mar 2022; v3 24 Jun 2022; v4 1 Aug 2022 (current). Later papers by the same author (2025, 2026) re-present and correct parts of this program; see those events.
events.delivers: Claims that every integral affine or projective scheme of finite presentation over a perfect field, in every dimension, admits a resolution. Since perfect fields of characteristic p are included, this covers positive characteristic for perfect base fields. It does not claim imperfect base fields. If the proof is correct it settles the bullet for perfect fields.
events.remains: Nothing, if the proof is correct. As of my reading, the 2025 paper (next event) says it restates only the first 8 sections of this paper, so the full argument as presented in the author's own later papers is not complete.
events.doubts: (1) The Proof Atlas reference list describes the 2022 preprint's all-dimensional claims as not validated, and says the collection 'did not verify peer-reviewed acceptance or independent validation'. (2) The author's 2025 paper (next event) says it 'represents the first 8 sections of arXiv:2203.03842', focusing entirely on Gr(3,n) rather than general Gr(d,n), with 'Part II... will follow'. (3) The author's 2026 paper 2609.24047 says it 'corrects and validates Chapters 5, 6 and 8' of the 2025 paper, without describing the corrections. These are the author's own statements and the reference list's; I did not read the 141-page text, so I cannot identify a specific error.
events.direction: Claims a full resolution theorem for perfect base fields in all dimensions; cuts in favour of resolution if the claim holds.

events.what_happened: Gergely Bérczi, Honglu Fan and Mingcong Zeng, 'An ML approach to resolution of singularities', arXiv 2307.00252 (v1 1 Jul 2023; v2 23 Aug 2023), for the ICML 2023 TAG workshop (PMLR 221). They recast the resolution process as the 'Hironaka game' and train reinforcement-learning agents to choose blowups that reduce polynomial additions in a symbolic-computation setting; they report a proof-of-concept against selection heuristics. The abstract treats existence of resolution as background and makes no claim about it.
events.delivers: No resolution result. A learning method for choosing blowups in an algorithm, with experiments in symbolic computation.
events.remains: The whole problem.

checked_by.who: ICML 2023 TAG workshop, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research vol. 221 (referees not named)

events.direction: Method only; neutral to the answer.

events.what_happened: Federico Castillo, Daniel Duarte, Maximiliano Leyton-Álvarez and Alvaro Liendo, 'Nash blowup fails to resolve singularities in dimensions four and higher', arXiv 2409.19767 (v1 29 Sep 2024; v2 4 Oct 2024; v3 7 Nov 2025). Abstract: iterating Nash blowups or normalised Nash blowups does not resolve singularities of varieties of dimension four or higher over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic. Comments: 'To appear in Annals of Mathematics.' A 2026 listing gives Annals 203(2) (search snippet, not opened).
events.delivers: Shows that one specific procedure, iterated (normalised) Nash blowups, fails to resolve singularities in dimension four and higher over algebraically closed fields of any characteristic. It does not concern blowups with chosen centres, and it does not decide whether resolution exists by any other means.
events.remains: The bullet's question, which this result leaves open because its scope is one procedure.

checked_by.who: Annals of Mathematics (acceptance indicated by the 'to appear' comment on arXiv)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted for publication, per the arXiv comment; the 2026 volume listing is a search snippet

events.direction: Cuts against the iterated Nash-blowup procedure in dimension four and up, not against the existence of resolution, by its own scope.
events.object: Toric varieties, per the conference abstract and search summaries, which the normalised and plain Nash-blowup iterations do not resolve in dimension four and up, in every characteristic. I did not read this from the paper body.

events.what_happened: Steven Dale Cutkosky (Missouri), talk 'Why is resolution of singularities so hard in characteristic p?', COMA Colloquium (SLMath), 20 March 2024. The abstract explains local uniformisation along a valuation and isolates where Zariski's reduction-of-multiplicity argument fails in characteristic p, namely defect in valuation extensions. The SLMath page says 'No Notes/Supplements Uploaded'; no written version found.
events.delivers: An analysis of the obstruction. The abstract states no new theorem.
events.remains: The whole problem.
events.direction: Neutral: locates the failure point of one classical argument.

events.what_happened: Hussein Mourtada and Bernd Schober, 'Teissier singularities', arXiv 2502.01239 (submitted 3 Feb 2025). The abstract states the note's goal: 'to introduce Teissier singularities and to explain why they are candidate to play, in positive characteristic, a role for resolution of singularities similar to the one quasi-ordinary singularities play in characteristic zero.' Published in Comptes Rendus Mathématique 363 (2025), 799–808, online 4 July 2025 (search listing, not opened). A companion paper on their resolution is listed as in preparation in search results.
events.revisions: Published in Comptes Rendus Mathématique (online 4 July 2025).
events.delivers: No resolution result. A new class of singularities proposed as a candidate for a resolution role in positive characteristic; the abstract states the motivational aim, not a theorem.
events.remains: The whole problem; the companion resolution paper was not found.

checked_by.who: Comptes Rendus Mathématique referees (not named in what I could read)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper, vol. 363 (2025), pp. 799–808 (search listing)

events.direction: Programmatic; neutral to the answer.

events.what_happened: Yi Hu, 'Universal Characteristic-free Resolution of Singularities, I', arXiv 2507.21400 (29 July 2025; v1 only; 162 pages). Abstract: 'We prove that for any singular integral affine variety X of finite presentation over a perfect field defined over Z, there exists a smooth morphism from Y onto X such that Y admits a resolution', followed by a smooth morphism Y to X. Comments: 'This paper represents the first 8 sections of arXiv:2203.03842 focusing entirely on Gr(3,n) instead of general Gr(d,n). Part II is straightforward and will follow.' A seminar series 'Universal Characteristic-free Resolution of Singularities' (speaker Yi Hu, 17 Dec 2025 to 9 Jan 2026, 8 sessions, Yau Mathematical Sciences Center, Tsinghua) states the aim 'To examine and verify the key details of the article'. The speaker is the author, so that seminar is not an independent check.
events.revisions: v1 only, as of my reading.
events.delivers: Claims a smooth cover Y to X of any singular integral affine finite-presentation X over a perfect field defined over Z, with Y admitting a resolution. Per its comments, the paper covers the Gr(3,n) part only. It is not a resolution of X itself, and it is a different formulation from the 2022 claim.
events.remains: The general Gr(d,n) case ('Part II', which I did not find posted), and a resolution of X itself rather than of a smooth cover Y.

checked_by.who: YMSC Tsinghua seminar led by the author, Yi Hu (author-led; not independent)
checked_by.qualification: The speaker is the paper's author; the seminar's stated purpose is verification, but no written outcome was found
checked_by.what_they_did: Eight-session seminar, 17 Dec 2025 to 9 Jan 2026, on the article

events.doubts: (1) The comments say the paper covers Gr(3,n) only and that Part II will follow. (2) The author's own 2026 paper 2609.24047 says it corrects and validates chapters 5, 6 and 8 of this paper, without describing the corrections. (3) The only seminar on it was run by the author, so it does not count as independent checking.
events.direction: Claims a restricted (Gr(3,n)) form of the 2022 program, stated as a smooth cover; cuts in favour of resolution only in that form.

events.what_happened: Castillo, Duarte, Leyton-Álvarez and Liendo, 'On a Computational Approach to the Nash Blowup Problem', arXiv 2511.17862 (v1 22 Nov 2025; v2 17 Aug 2026). The paper describes the implementation behind the Nash counterexamples, gives further toric varieties not resolved by normalised Nash blowups, and reports tens of thousands of two-dimensional and millions of three-dimensional toric varieties resolved by iterated Nash blowups, presented as evidence rather than proof.
events.delivers: Computational evidence and further toric counterexamples for Nash-blowup procedures. Concerns those procedures only.
events.remains: The whole problem.
events.direction: Concerns the Nash-blowup procedure only; neutral to the answer.

events.what_happened: Michel Brion (Institut Fourier, Grenoble), colloquium at TIFR on 8 Dec 2025. The abstract notes that equivariant resolution, which holds in characteristic zero, 'fails in positive characteristics, already for curves', and proposes 'a notion of equivariant regularity as a remedy'. Only the colloquium abstract is in the sources; I found no arXiv write-up.
events.delivers: No result on the bullet's question. It concerns resolutions compatible with group actions (equivariant resolution), a different question.
events.remains: The whole problem.
events.direction: Different question (equivariant resolution); outside scope.

events.what_happened: Gergely Bérczi (Aarhus University), 'Evolving Ranking Functions for Canonical Blow-Ups in Positive Characteristic', arXiv 2602.06553 (6 Feb 2026; v1 only; math.AG with cs.LG cross-list). The paper reports computer search for ranking functions for a toy canonical blow-up process in dimension 4, characteristic 3, for hypersurfaces with a monic purely inseparable leading term. The search used the AlphaEvolve evolutionary search system, and the author's experiments were 'vibe-coded using a mixture of large language models'. Results reported: a two-component ranker from a run of 26 hours (on a 71-case focused benchmark); a five-component lexicographic tuple, then a discretised version from a run of about 24 hours; an explicit counterexample, credited to GPT 5.2 Pro, showing the first tuple does not extend beyond its family; and two conjectures (Conjecture 1 for the family z³ + g + z²h, window m = 5 empirically; Conjecture 2 for the discretised ranker on a 100-case benchmark), supported by finite computation only.
events.revisions: v1 only, as of my reading.
events.delivers: No resolution, and no termination theorem. It gives conjectural delayed ranking functions (candidate termination certificates for a canonical blow-up process) for dimension 4, characteristic 3, monic purely inseparable hypersurfaces in the family z³ + g + z²h, supported by computation. The paper says that no general ranking function is known in positive characteristic.
events.remains: The whole problem, including the conjectures themselves, which the paper states are unproved.
events.directly_checkable: The explicit counterexample hypersurface quoted in the paper, z³ + x¹² + y⁶ + w⁹y⁴ + x⁹y⁸w¹⁰, can be checked against the stated ranker's conditions by hand. The counterexample's proof is a computer simulation described in the paper as a 'proof sketch', so the search results themselves are not hand-checkable.
events.doubts: The search outputs depend on an evaluation harness written and edited by the author with LLM help. The author says the code was 'then repeatedly checked and edited for basic invariance properties, and to eliminate errors'. The conjectures are labelled 'working conjecture' in the paper and have finite evidence only.
events.direction: Neither proves nor disproves resolution. It gives conjectural candidates in a restricted setting, and a counterexample showing one candidate fails outside its family.
events.object: Candidate ranking functions found by AlphaEvolve: a two-component ranker (26-hour run), a five-component lexicographic tuple (c1 to c5), and a discretised ranker Π∘R. These are conjectural termination certificates for a toy blow-up process on the family z³ + g + z²h (dimension 4, characteristic 3), checked on finite benchmarks of 71 and then 100 cases. Separately, the hypersurface z³ + x¹² + y⁶ + w⁹y⁴ + x⁹y⁸w¹⁰ (credited to GPT 5.2 Pro) is an explicit counterexample showing that the lexicographic tuple does not give bounded-delay descent for arbitrary inputs with the same parameters. Both are explicit. Neither is a counterexample to resolution.

systems.name: AlphaEvolve
systems.what_it_did: Searched for candidate ranking functions. Per the author, 'After 26 hours AlphaEvolve found ... a pure two-component ranking function' on the focused benchmark; in a later run 'After approximately 44 hours, AlphaEvolve discovered a new five-component raw rank function'. The author wrote the explicit tuple, built a counterexample, and set up the discretised version with a further run of about 24 hours. Conjecture 2 is stated in terms of a ranker the paper says was discovered by AlphaEvolve.
systems.basis_quote: AlphaEvolve is used solely to search for ranking functions.

systems.name: GPT 5.2 Pro
systems.what_it_did: Found the explicit hypersurface counterexample z³ + x¹² + y⁶ + w⁹y⁴ + x⁹y⁸w¹⁰, which the paper uses to show that the candidate lexicographic tuple does not extend beyond its family. The paper's numbering of this lemma differs between two readings of the same HTML (Lemma 1 and Lemma 2).
systems.basis_quote: Here is a counterexample we found using GPT 5.2 Pro for m=10.

ai.disclosed_cost: No cost or token figures. Compute is stated only as run durations: 'roughly eleven experiments, with runtimes ranging from 33 hours to 22 days', with specific runs of 26 hours, about 24 hours and about 44 hours mentioned.

events.what_happened: Proof Atlas, which describes itself as 'AI-first mathematical research · exact proof evidence', hosts a collaboration workspace for this problem, stated as 'whether every integral finite-type variety of dimension at least four over a perfect field of characteristic p admits a proper birational resolution by a regular variety'. The page marks the problem as open, records 'Status checked: Aug 6, 2026' and 'Source recorded: Aug 7, 2026', and says 'All claims remain provisional narrative evidence rather than independently checked proofs'. It says a Mathlib search 'did not verify an exact formal statement or checked proof'. Its 22 references include Hironaka 1964, Cossart–Piltant 2008, 2009 and 2019, de Jong 1996, Hauser 2010, Hauser–Perlega 2024, Hironaka 2017, Yi Hu 2022, Bérczi 2026 and Castillo et al. 2026. It does not list Tian's arXiv 2608.20066, which was posted after the status check.
events.delivers: A status record, not a result. It marks the problem open and records its reference list.
events.remains: The whole problem.
events.doubts: The workspace itself says its claims are provisional and not independently checked. Its creator is not identified on the page I read. Its 'Trust' section was not readable.
events.direction: None; status only.

events.what_happened: Yi Hu, 'Introduction to Universal Equations and Characteristic-free Resolution', arXiv 2608.10272 (v1 10 Aug 2026; v2 22 Sep 2026). The abstract opens: 'Recently, we announced a proof of a characteristic-free resolution of singularities. This is a survey article on the proof.' The comments say the 2609.24047 paper corrects and validates chapters 5, 6 and 8 of 2507.21400. Where and when the 'announcement' took place is not stated in the sources I read.
events.delivers: An expository account of the claimed characteristic-free proof. It states no new theorem in the abstract or comments I read. The claim is 'characteristic-free', which by its wording covers all characteristics, but the page does not elaborate.
events.remains: Nothing new is established by this text on its own.
events.doubts: A survey by the same author of the same claim. The 'announcement' it refers to was not located.
events.direction: Claims a characteristic-free resolution (expository); cuts in favour if that claim holds.

events.what_happened: Chenxiao Tian (sole author; Princeton affiliation given in a search snippet and not seen on the page I read), 'Resolution of Singularities in Positive Characteristic: Frobenius-Hasse Towers and Exceptional-History Descent', arXiv 2608.20066 (v1 20 Aug 2026; math.GM; the arXiv comment reads '798 pages in nine parts' and 'Comments are welcome'). Abstract as fetched: for a perfect field k of characteristic p>0, 'We introduce an object-level construction for canonical strong embedded resolution and principalization over k'; termination is by a 'strict multiset replacement' in a dependent well-founded order, after which 'the exhausted state reconstructs a regular strict transform'. The companion Google Sites page ('positive char resolution') calls the nine parts 'a single proof in four layers' covering arbitrary dimension, and lists finite termination, terminal regularity, normal crossings, strong principalization, reduced embedded resolution and functoriality as conclusions. Its collected edition (Parts I–IX, August 2026, 798 pp.) is on Google Drive, which I could not read. Its acknowledgements say: 'The author acknowledges the role of computer-assisted methods in the development of this project.' and 'All explicit examples, counterexamples, and accompanying code are available upon request.' A SSRN posting of the same title, dated 17 Aug 2026 in a search snippet, refused access (403).
events.revisions: Only v1 as of my reading. Companion notes on the project page are separate Drive files (Notes I to IV).
events.delivers: Claimed: canonical strong embedded resolution and principalization over a perfect field of characteristic p>0 in arbitrary dimension, which if correct yields resolution of varieties in every dimension over perfect base fields. The abstract does not claim imperfect base fields. The fetched abstract describes the 'object-level realization' of its certificate as formulated rather than established; I could not read the full text to confirm this wording.
events.remains: Nothing, if the claim holds. I could not read the 798-page text, so I cannot say which steps are established and which are only sketched.
events.doubts: (1) No peer review, expert endorsement, public comment, or citing work found in 54 days of searching. (2) Explicit examples and code are 'available upon request', not public. (3) The 'computer-assisted methods' acknowledgement names no method or system. (4) The Proof Atlas workspace that the project page links to, status checked 6 Aug 2026 before this preprint, marks the problem open and calls its claims provisional; it does not mention Tian. (5) The arXiv category is math.GM (general mathematics), not math.AG. (6) The reference list cites earlier parts as 'interface-only companion preprints' that I could not find. (7) The terminology is idiosyncratic ('Hasse packets', 'differential–integral saturation', 'global replacement certificate' in search summaries), and I could not map it to the standard literature. These are observations, not a verdict.
events.direction: Claims a complete resolution theorem for perfect base fields in every dimension; cuts in favour of resolution for those fields if correct. It claims nothing for imperfect fields.

events.what_happened: Yi Hu, 'Fundamental Lemmas in Universal Resolution', arXiv 2609.24047 (v1 21 Sep 2026; 22 pages). The abstract reads: 'We abstract and prove some fundamental lemmas in universal blowups.' The comments say: 'This paper corrects and validates Chapters 5, 6 and 8 of https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21400.'
events.delivers: Lemmas on universal blowups which the comments say correct and validate three chapters of 2507.21400. It claims no resolution in the abstract or comments.
events.remains: The rest of the universal program, including Part II of 2507.21400 and the general case.
events.doubts: The author's own note says chapters 5, 6 and 8 of 2507.21400 needed correction and validation; the nature of the earlier errors is not described in the abstract or comments I read.
events.direction: Partial, lemma-level; neutral to the answer.

disputes.summary: Whether Hironaka claimed a proof in 2008. Woit's post relays talks 'claiming to have a proof' for any dimension; commenter Terry Hughes says it was 'a vast overstatement' and Hironaka 'made no claims that he solved the problem'; Woit's update says his source was 'most likely overly optimistic'. The 2017 manuscript that Wikipedia says 'claims to prove' existence is a separate written claim.

Cossart–Piltant's threefold result: Wikipedia says it holds 'in all characteristics'; the HAL abstract restricts Parts I and II to fields differentially finite over a perfect subfield. The 2014/2019 arithmetical paper removes that restriction for dimension 3.

Yi Hu's claims change form between 2022 and 2025. The 2022 abstract says 'X admits a resolution' for every integral finite-presentation scheme over a perfect field. The 2025 abstract says only that there is a smooth morphism Y to X with Y admitting a resolution, and its comments limit the paper to the Gr(3,n) part, 'the first 8 sections' of the 2022 paper.

Authorship and date of the Hauser–Perlega surface result. The 2024 Publ. RIMS paper is by Hauser and Perlega, submitted 16 Feb 2022; the 2020 arXiv 2011.14443 is by Perlega alone and treats the same subject. I have not verified that they contain the same argument, so the earliest public written argument could be 2020 or the 2024 publication.

Tian (arXiv 2608.20066, Aug 2026, 'a single proof' for all dimensions over perfect fields) and Hu (arXiv 2203.03842, Mar 2022, all integral finite-presentation schemes over perfect fields, and the 2025–26 series) each claim a general resolution theorem for perfect fields. Neither has been checked by an independent reader in the sources I found, and the two claims are not reconciled by any source.

summary: Since 26 January 2024, no accepted or independently checked work settles this problem. The bullet asks for resolution of singularities over fields of characteristic p in all dimensions; the Wikipedia lead states the open case as dimension at least 4 over fields of characteristic p, with dimensions 1 to 3 known (Abhyankar 1956 and 1966, Lipman 1978, Cutkosky 2006, Cossart–Piltant 2008–09 and 2014/2019). Three in-window developments need weighing. (1) Chenxiao Tian's 798-page preprint (arXiv 2608.20066, 20 Aug 2026) claims canonical strong embedded resolution and principalization over perfect fields of characteristic p in arbitrary dimension. The abstract and the project page describe a complete proof, but I could not read the 798 pages (the PDF, the Drive copy and SSRN were all unreadable to me), and I found no review, endorsement or citing work in 54 days. The acknowledgement says 'computer-assisted methods' were used, without naming a method or system; the project page links to Proof Atlas, an 'AI-first' workspace that lists the problem as open and whose status check (6 Aug 2026) predates the preprint. I record that as a disclosed but undescribed possible AI role, not as an established one; the field 'none_found' is false for that reason. (2) Yi Hu's 2022 preprint (arXiv 2203.03842) claims resolution of every integral finite-presentation scheme over a perfect field, all dimensions. It has never been published or independently checked as far as I can find. The author's own 2025 preprint restates only its first 8 sections (Gr(3,n) only, with 'Part II' still to come), and the author's Sept 2026 paper says it corrects chapters 5, 6 and 8 of that 2025 paper. The one seminar on the 2025 paper was run by Hu, so it is not an independent check. (3) Gergely Bérczi's 2026 preprint (arXiv 2602.06553) is the clearest AI-involved event. It uses AlphaEvolve to search for candidate ranking functions for a toy blow-up process in dimension 4, characteristic 3, and GPT 5.2 Pro to find a counterexample lemma; its declaration says 'a variety of AI-based tools were used extensively throughout the project' and that 'the mathematical conclusions, conjectures, and counterexamples presented here arise from independent mathematical analysis'. The output is two conjectures with finite computational support and no resolution claim. Several other events are discounted by scope: the Nash-blowup counterexamples (Castillo et al. 2024 and 2025) concern one procedure, not existence; Hauser–Perlega's 2018 cycle paper concerns a residual-order invariant and its authors say it is not a counterexample to resolution; Mourtada–Schober (2025) is a programme; Brion (2025) and Cutkosky (2024) are talks on related questions. The Tian and Hu claims are both for perfect base fields only; the bullet does not say perfect, so the imperfect case is also not covered by either. Close calls: whether Tian's text, if correct, settles the bullet for perfect fields (the bullet's own wording does not restrict to perfect fields); whether the Hu 2022 claim or the Tian claim should be read as the event the problem's status rests on; and whether the Bérczi AlphaEvolve output is load-bearing, since its conjectures are the paper's main results but are conjectural. All of these are for the later pass.
competing_reading: Read the Tian preprint as settling the perfect-field case: it is a single-author, 798-page proof whose author states it as complete, posted in August 2026; if it is correct, the bullet is resolved for perfect fields and the status is 'solved', with the earlier Hu 2022 claim as an earlier unverified version of the same answer. Against this: nothing I could read supports or refutes the proof, and the status 'solved' would rest on a claim no expert has yet checked. For Bérczi: read the AlphaEvolve and GPT 5.2 Pro output as load-bearing mathematics, since the discretised ranker and the counterexample lemma are in the paper's theorems-and-conjectures section and the author credits the machine with discovering the ranking functions that the conjectures state. Against this: the paper states its results as conjectures with finite evidence, no theorem depends on the AI output, and the author says the conclusions are his own analysis.
what_would_settle_it: (a) Expert written assessments of arXiv 2608.20066 (especially its termination theorem and the object-level realisation), or a referee report; (b) a published verification or specific error report for Hu's arXiv 2203.03842 and its 2025–2026 corrections, including Part II; (c) the full text of the Tian manuscript with its acknowledgements read, to determine what 'computer-assisted methods' means and whether any AI system is named; (d) a Lean or Coq formalisation of either claim with its sorry status, which I did not find; (e) the Bérczi paper's conjectures being proved or refuted, and an authors' statement on whether any theorem uses the AlphaEvolve output beyond the conjecture; (f) Proof Atlas's creator and the status of its Trust section.

incomplete: (1) The Tian manuscript (798 pages, arXiv 2608.20066) was not read. The arXiv PDF and the Drive copy returned binary or unreadable content, the arXiv HTML is only about 11,000 characters, and SSRN returned 403. So the proof, its stated scope and its acknowledgements are reported from the abstract, the project page and search snippets only. The search snippet claiming that the acknowledgements thank Princeton research resources conflicts with the HTML reading, which found no acknowledgements; I could not settle which is right. The Tian affiliation (Princeton) comes only from a search snippet. (2) Hu's 2022 paper (141 pages) and 2025 paper (162 pages) were read from the abstract page and comments only; their proofs, their AI disclosures (if any) and their correction notes were not read. The 2609.24047 correction is described in its comments only. (3) The Hironaka 2017 manuscript was unreadable (binary PDF), so its scope rests on Wikipedia and the Proof Atlas reference list. (4) Cossart–Piltant Parts I and II were not opened, and the HAL deposit date was unavailable, so their dates are journal years. (5) Hauser–Perlega (Publ. RIMS 2024) full text was not read; whether it is the same argument as Perlega's 2020 arXiv 2011.14443 is unverified. (6) The Bérczi quotes come from a model-rendered view of the arXiv HTML; I read both halves of the page, but the wording should be checked against the arXiv source before the record is used for exact quotations. The GPT 5.2 Pro counterexample is numbered Lemma 1 in one reading and Lemma 2 in another. (7) The Spivakovsky date is a month from an undated page, and the Hironaka 2008 date is the date of the blog report, not of any talk. Dates for Abhyankar (1956, 1966), Lipman (1978) and de Jong (1996) come from Wikipedia rather than the originals. (8) The Proof Atlas workspace's creator and its 'Trust' section were not identified or read. (9) Only one formalisation query was run, with no hits; Mathlib and Lean repositories were not searched directly. (10) The search covered arXiv only through the search tool, not through arXiv listings by date, so events posted but not indexed would be missed. (11) Tsinghua lectures by Hu (June–July 2026) and Hu's 2021 talk are recorded as listings; they are not counted as events because they are not written arguments.
